CausalChain: HCC cells overexpress PCSK9 -> Elevated PCSK9 increases degradation of MHC I molecules on tumor cell surfaces -> Reduced MHC I expression leads to impaired antigen presentation -> Diminished CD8+ T-cell recognition enables immune evasion -> PCSK9 inhibition restores MHC I expression -> Enhanced antigen presentation improves CD8+ T-cell activity -> Combined with PD-1 blockade, this results in synergistic anti-tumor immune response
Hypothesis: In HCC, PCSK9-driven degradation of MHC class I molecules contributes to immune evasion; therefore, inhibiting PCSK9 will restore MHC class I expression and antigen presentation, thereby synergizing with PD-1 blockade to improve anti-tumor immunity and patient outcomes.
Abstract: The rising incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its frequent resistance to conventional immunotherapies highlight an urgent need to better understand the mechanisms that drive immune escape in these tumors. Recent emerging evidence links the proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) not only to lipid metabolism but also to immune regulation. Our hypothesis proposes that in HCC, overexpression of PCSK9 promotes degradation of cell‐surface MHC class I molecules, thereby reducing tumor antigen presentation and leading to diminished CD8+ T‐cell recognition. Inhibition of PCSK9 may restore MHC class I expression, enhancing antigen presentation and ultimately sensitize tumors to immune checkpoint blockade such as anti‐PD-1 therapy. Combining a PCSK9 inhibitor with PD-1 blockade could synergistically improve anti-tumor responses by reactivating suppressed cytotoxic T lymphocyte functions in HCC patients.
